label: Copy phase, mid-sequence recall with o/3/2/p/g being output now or next
predicate: (phase == 2) & (recall_idx >= 2) & (isin(out_tok, [tok("o"), tok("3"), tok("2"), tok("p"), tok("g")]) | isin(next_out, [tok("o"), tok("3"), tok("2"), tok("p"), tok("g")]))
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase feature (99.8% of mass). It does not fire in the original phase or at the delimiter, and almost never on recall_idx 0-1. Activity peaks at recall_idx 3-4 (rate 28-35%) and drops off later. Within the copy phase, the output token identity modulates it strongly: o (64% rate), 3 (60%), 2 (49%), p (35%), g (30%), then a long tail (r, l, c, z). The upcoming next_out shows the same token preference, so activations often begin a step before one of these tokens is output. The largest activations (about 1.0) occur when o is output right after p/d, especially when there are runs of o. Lower-quartile activations are spread over other output tokens in the middle of the copy, so the token set is a graded preference, not a hard boundary. Dev F1 is about 0.62 with mass recall 0.78; precision is limited because many in-set steps stay silent.
